attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own newsletter post, published under his name.

semantics.note: The sentence comes right after the passage on chatbot-associated deaths and lawsuits, so reading 'it' as that problem is fair. It is a firm present-tense observation with no hedge.

contract.note: Marcus named no measure. Reading 'worse' as more reported deaths and lawsuits in 2025 than in 2023–2024 is the ordinary reading, given that he cites lawsuits and new cases. A per-user rate is unmeasurable, so the result rests on the reported-case reading.

evidence.note: AP, Nov 2025: seven suits filed in one day, four of them over suicides. This shows reported deaths and suits rising sharply in late 2025.
WSJ, Dec 2025: dozens of cases have emerged since spring 2025, including several suicides and a murder, and they led to a series of wrongful-death suits.
CBS, Jan 15 2026: a new suit over Gordon's death in Nov 2025. Shows new cases kept appearing up to the post date.
Compiled case list, available on the evaluation date. Gives the baseline: a few cases in 2023–2024 and several dated cases in 2025.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading (more reported deaths and suits), the evidence shows a few cases in 2023–2024. 2025 into January 2026 brought many more, including a batch of suits in November 2025 and the Gordon case. The packet has no evidence of a flat or falling count. One caveat: part of the rise may reflect more users and more attention.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. He mentions Hill's reporting but asserts the growing problem himself.

semantics.note: 'Apparently' qualifies whether chatbots cause the delusions, not the trend. 'Growing problem' is a firm observation, so the claim is scorable.

contract.note: Marcus himself ties the problem to cases Hill and others have documented, so measuring it by documented cases follows his own words. Not requiring proof of causation respects his 'apparently'.

evidence.note: Aarhus health-records study, covering records up to June 2025: a clear rise over time in record entries on harmful chatbot use, mainly worsened delusions. Published after the post but before the evaluation date.
WSJ, Dec 2025: psychiatrists reviewed dozens of cases in the past nine months and increasingly see a link. Consistent with growth during 2025.

The study's lead author says part of the rise reflects greater awareness, yet still calls the problem under-detected. This qualifies the size of the rise but does not show documented cases were flat or falling.

reviews.rationale: A health-records study shows documented cases of harmful chatbot use, mainly worsened delusions, rising up to mid-2025. Psychiatrists quoted by the WSJ report dozens of cases since spring 2025. The awareness caveat limits how much of this is true growth, but it does not contradict the rise in documented cases, which is how Marcus framed it.
